traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality & Specificity: Every relevant rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) defines concrete meta.messages entries that explain exactly what is wrong (missing annotation, invalid format, missing file/requirement, invalid path) and includes dynamic data (function/req/story path). Tests assert messageId and data wiring for each rule.
- Quality & ESLint Best Practices: Rules use ESLint’s messageId + meta.messages patterns, with placeholders like {{name}}, {{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, and {{storyPath}}. RuleTester-based suites confirm integration with ESLint’s reporting model.
- Integration & Severity: src/index.ts maps rules to severities consistent with the story (errors for missing annotations and references, warn for formatting issues). plugin-default-export-and-configs tests validate the recommended/strict flat-config presets, including [REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY] assertions.
- User Experience (problem, location, suggested fix): - Function rules: require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation messages embed the function name, with reportMissing choosing the identifier node for location. error-reporting.test.ts verifies suggestions for require-story-annotation include a clear desc and fix function. - Branch rule: message “Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.” pinpoints which annotation is missing and auto-fix tests show inserted placeholder comments, guiding the developer. - File and requirement rules: valid-story-reference and valid-req-reference messages embed the offending path/ID and differentiate causes (missing file, invalid extension, invalid path, missing requirement, filesystem error).
- Error Handling & Edge Cases: The implementation explicitly handles incomplete context: anonymous functions get a fallback name, filesystem errors are converted to safe error messages instead of crashing, and invalid rule configuration is reported via an explicit diagnostic rather than throwing. Dedicated tests validate these behaviors (e.g., “Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling” and the annotation-checker/require-req-annotation suites).
- Documentation & Conventions: The story file documents intended conventions; the implementation follows the patterns (even if some internal placeholder names differ, e.g., {{path}} vs the example {{filePath}}). All rules are annotated with @story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md and appropriate REQ-ERROR-* tags, and tests explicitly reference this story in headers.
Given the concrete rule implementations, story-linked tests, and successful full test run, this story is fully implemented and verified.
